actions.action: Inspect leaf junctions and undersides with a flashlight to tell bugs from residue
Touch flecks to check whether they smear (residue) or are cottony bugs
Rinse foliage with plain water to remove spray residue
Spot-treat each visible bug with 70% isopropyl alcohol on a cotton swab, repeated every 5-7 days for 3-4 weeks
Isolate the plant from other plants during treatment
Remove badly damaged, mostly brown leaves
Check the roots if the plant keeps declining
If mealybugs persist, apply a systemic imidacloprid houseplant insecticide to the soil

reason: The answer identifies a sap-sucking pest infestation (mealybugs, which fit 'or similar bugs') as the main cause, and its core fix of wiping the bugs off with alcohol and cutting bad leaves matches what worked; nothing it recommends is likely to hurt the plant.
